summary: Describes the Diameter Quality-of-Service application, in which network elements interact with Diameter servers when allocating QoS resources. It defines two modes, pull and push. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: A network box asks a boss for permission to give someone a fast lane, or the boss tells it to set one up.

questions: what is the diameter qos application
diameter qos pull mode vs push mode
subtitle: How routers ask a Diameter server for permission to reserve network quality of service, or get told to install it.

tldr.problem: Routers that grant quality-of-service resources need a way to check, through AAA infrastructure, that a request is authorized, and sometimes a server needs to configure the router without being asked.
tldr.mechanism: The Diameter QoS application defines Pull mode, where the Network Element sends a QoS-Authorization-Request, and Push mode, where the Authorizing Entity sends a QoS-Install-Request, plus re-authorization, termination and accounting hooks.
tldr.outcome: One Diameter QoS server can support both modes with two new command codes, 326 and 327, under Application-Id 9, and two new AVPs.

today: RFC 5866 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2010. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Diameter QoS Application Does
sections.content:
The Diameter QoS application lets Network Elements (NEs) interact with Diameter servers when allocating QoS resources in the network. It defines two modes. In Pull mode the NE requests QoS authorization from the server, triggered by something on the data path such as a QoS signaling protocol. In Push mode the server proactively sends a command that installs QoS authorization state in the NE, which could be triggered by off-path signaling such as SIP call control.

A single set of command codes allows one Diameter QoS server to support both modes, depending on network technology, deployment scenario and end-host capabilities. The document uses the AVPs defined in RFC 5777 and RFC 5624 and builds on the Diameter base protocol of RFC 3588.
sections.eli5: Either the router asks the boss, 'may I give this person a fast lane?', or the boss walks over and says, 'set up a fast lane for this person'.

sections.title: Roles and Framework
sections.content:
The application runs between an NE acting as a Diameter client and an Authorizing Entity (AE) acting as a Diameter server, with a cloud of AAA servers in between. The NE corresponds to a Policy Enforcement Point and the AE to a Policy Decision Point. The end-host side is described with an Application Endpoint, an Application Server, and a Resource Requesting Entity (RRE) that triggers the QoS interaction. The RRE is only indirectly involved: the Diameter exchange runs between the NE and the AE.

Which mode applies depends on the endpoint. A Category 1 endpoint has no QoS capability, and a Category 2 endpoint only at the application level; for both, Push mode is REQUIRED. A Category 3 endpoint has network-level QoS capability and either mode MAY be used. Push suits networks such as cable, DSL, Ethernet and Diffserv-enabled IP/MPLS, while Pull suits IntServ-enabled IP networks or certain wireless networks such as GPRS. Some networks, such as WiMAX, may need both.

Pull mode has a two-party scheme (no Diameter QoS exchange needed) and two three-party schemes, the basic one and a token-based one in which an authorization token obtained earlier is presented along with the request. The RFC also lists requirements the application must meet, among them identity-based routing, dynamic authorization, bearer gating and failure notification, and asks that three kinds of session (QoS signaling, Diameter authorization and application-layer) be correlated, with the AE SHOULD binding them together.
sections.eli5: There is a doorman (the router), a manager (the server) and a visitor asking for a fast lane. Visitors who cannot ask for themselves need the manager to call the doorman first.

sections.title: Pull and Push Session Setup
sections.content:
The mode is chosen by the first message. When the AE receives a QoS-Authorization-Request (QAR) with a new Session-Id it operates in Pull mode, and when the NE receives a QoS-Install-Request (QIR) with a new Session-Id it operates in Push mode.

In Pull mode, a QoS reservation request or local event makes the NE convert the QoS signaling objects into AVPs and send a QAR. The server decides the authorized resources and flow state (enabled or disabled) and answers with a QoS-Authorization-Answer (QAA). A successful first answer carries the result DIAMETER_LIMITED_SUCCESS, meaning the AE expects a later QAR to confirm the reservation and the final reserved resources. That confirming QAR is answered with DIAMETER_SUCCESS. The answer also carries an authorization lifetime, and extending it SHOULD be done with a new QAR/QAA exchange.

In Push mode, the server is triggered by application-layer signaling or a local event and sends a QIR to the NE. The NE installs the state and replies with a QoS-Install-Answer (QIA), carrying DIAMETER_SUCCESS on success. The AE needs to know which NE to contact and for which flow, through static configuration or dynamic discovery. If several AEs control the same NE, the NE should choose which decision to enforce based on the priority of the request.
sections.eli5: In Pull, the doorman phones the manager and waits for a yes. In Push, the manager phones the doorman and says what to do, and the doorman reports back that it is done.

sections.title: Re-Authorization, Termination and Accounting
sections.content:
Re-authorization can start on either side. The NE MAY send a new QAR at any time before the authorization period ends, for example when QoS signaling asks to change an ongoing session. The AE MAY send a Re-Auth-Request (RAR) from the Diameter base protocol; the NE acknowledges with a Re-Auth-Answer (RAA). If the RAR carries no parameters of the new QoS state, the NE MUST start re-authorization by sending a QAR.

Termination also works from both sides. The NE MAY send a Session-Termination-Request (STR) and receive an STA, for instance when a signaling message deletes the reservation or soft state expires. The AE MAY send an Abort-Session-Request (ASR), for example because of insufficient credits or the end of the application session, which releases the reserved resources at the NE.

For accounting, the NE MAY start an accounting session with an Accounting-Request after a successful reservation, send interim messages after re-authorization, and send a final exchange after termination. Authorization and accounting sessions are managed independently. Detailed QoS accounting procedures are out of scope.
sections.eli5: Either side can say 'let us check again' or 'stop now'. The doorman can also keep a tally of how long the fast lane was used.

sections.title: Commands and Application-Id
sections.content:
Four new Diameter messages are defined. The QAR and QAA share command code 326, and the QIR and QIA share command code 327. The request has the 'R' bit set and the answer has it cleared. The application also reuses base protocol commands: RAR/RAA (258), ASR/ASA (274) and STR/STA (275).

The value 9 MUST be used as the Application-Id in all QAR/QAA and QIR/QIA commands, while zero SHOULD be used in STR/STA, ASR/ASA and RAR/RAA. Nodes MAY advertise support by including 9 in the Auth-Application-Id or Acct-Application-Id AVP of the capabilities exchange.

Each message is defined in the modified ABNF of Diameter. A QAR, for instance, requires Session-Id, Auth-Application-Id, Origin-Host, Origin-Realm, Destination-Realm and Auth-Request-Type, and may carry Destination-Host, User-Name, QoS-Resources and QoS-Authorization-Data. The QoS application also has its own state machine based on the base protocol's authorization state machine, with extra states for server-initiated Push mode.
sections.eli5: Each kind of phone call has a number: one for 'may I?' calls and one for 'please do this' calls, and every call says which program it belongs to.

sections.title: QoS Application AVPs
sections.content:
The application reuses base protocol AVPs such as Session-Id, Origin-Host, Destination-Host, Result-Code and User-Name, and the QoS AVPs of RFC 5777, including QoS-Resources. It adds two AVPs, both with the M (mandatory) bit set and the V bit not set.

  • QoS-Authorization-Data (AVP code 579, OctetString): a container for application-session or user-specific data that the AE needs to compute the authorization decision.
  • Bound-Auth-Session-Id (AVP code 580, UTF8String): the ID of the Diameter authentication session used for network access, tying a QoS request to an earlier authentication of the end-host at the NE.

The Auth-Application-Id for the Diameter QoS application is 9. IANA allocated the two AVP codes, the application ID and command codes 326 and 327.
sections.eli5: Two new form fields were added: one for a note that helps the manager decide, and one for linking this request to an earlier sign-in.

sections.title: Worked Call Flows
sections.content:
The RFC gives three examples, each starting with SIP signaling between the end-host, a SIP proxy that acts as the Diameter QoS server, and a correspondent node.

In the Pull success case, the host sends a QoS NSLP Reserve with a QSPEC and authorization data. The first QoS-aware NE puts the AE identity in Destination-Host, the session data in QoS-Authorization-Data and the QoS description in QoS-Resources, and sends a QAR. The QAA returns the Result-Code, authorized QoS-Resources and the Authorization-Lifetime, and the NE installs the state and forwards the Reserve.

In the Pull failure case, the QAA carries the permanent error DIAMETER_AUTHORIZATION_REJECTED (5003). The NE stops the reservation downstream and returns an error to the host with an INFO_SPEC object indicating Authorization failure (0x02).

In the Push example the server uses a two-stage commit. A QIR first prepares the reservation without activating it. When the 200 OK arrives, the server sends a RAR to activate the installed policies and commit the allocation.
sections.eli5: The examples show a phone call setting up a video chat: first the manager says yes or no to the fast lane, and in the push version the lane is prepared first and switched on when the other person picks up.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC covers four components of security between the AE and the NE: authentication, authorization, integrity and confidentiality. Without authentication of the sender, an attacker could pose as a legitimate AE to allocate, change or free resources, or cause denial of service, for example by setting allowed bandwidth to zero or giving the whole bandwidth to a single flow. Without authenticating the NE, an attacker could give the AE a wrong view of network resource use. Failures to provide credentials should be logged.

Integrity protects Diameter messages from malicious alteration, and confidentiality prevents eavesdropping and traffic analysis when messages cross untrusted networks. Messages may carry authorization tokens that need confidentiality protection. Diameter offers communication security between neighboring peers using TLS or IPsec; authorization capabilities are application specific.
sections.eli5: If anyone could phone the doorman pretending to be the manager, they could hand out or block fast lanes, so both sides must prove who they are and keep their calls private.
